key_insight: Specialized, physics-driven machine learning force fields are needed to make ML interatomic potentials reliable for complex materials dynamics beyond near-equilibrium settings.
engineering_relevance: For fracture and damage modeling, task-specific MLIPs can extend atomistic simulation to larger scales and more realistic failure processes, but they must be validated against the exact observables of interest.
method: Compare universal pretrained equivariant GNN force fields with specialized, physics-informed adaptations.
Target demanding dynamical settings: electrified interfaces, open compositionally fluctuating systems, multiphase evolution, and large-scale fracture.
Use observable-specific benchmarking to judge whether the force field captures the intended materials behavior.
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes performance trade-offs and benchmarking needs across four challenging application contexts rather than presenting a single new dataset.
watch_item: High-order message passing, undersampled strained states, and missing nonlocal interactions can limit accuracy and increase computational cost in real fracture simulations.
paper_title: Specialized machine learning force fields for materials dynamics
